title: Intraoperative VIM thalamus microelectrode recordings during transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS) for essential tremor (Luu et al.; derivative: authors' processed 48 kHz signals)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the ventral intermediate (VIM) thalamus region of 9 adults with medication-refractory essential tremor undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. At each recording depth, 60 s were recorded with and without transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS), a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation therapy applied to the treated hand. This derivative release contains the authors' processed, software-filtered 48 kHz signals repackaged in BIDS (BrainVision format) with depth, stimulation settings and artifact-mask annotations.
methods_description: Recordings were made with FHC Guideline 4000 LP+ systems using anterior, center and posterior Ben-gun microelectrodes, each recorded bipolar against a macro contact 1 cm dorsal to the tip. 60 s trials were acquired at each depth without and with TAPS. The authors' processing low-pass filtered the signals, removed offsets, trimmed each trial to 60 s and computed motion-artifact blanking masks. The processed values were then stored as float32 BrainVision files.
